children: Our Bureau Mumbai: The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (Trai) has mandated telecom operators to offer affordable tariff plans for consumers seeking voice and SMS services without bundled data, despite opposition from operators. The regulator on Monday released the Telecom Consumer Protection (Thirteenth Amendment) Regulations, 2026.

Under the new rules, operators will have to offer special tariff vouchers (STVs) for voice and SMS with validity periods corresponding to each 30-day period and periods shorter than 30 days. They will also have to offer a voice-and-SMS STV that can be renewed on the same date every month. In addition, operators will have to offer at least one such STV with a validity longer than these periods.

The decision follows opposition from Reliance Jio, Bharti Airtel and Vodafone Idea during the consultation process. The operators argued that mandatory voice-and-SMS-only plans would be counterproductive. Jio argued that standalone voice plans were technically incompatible with modern 4G and 5G networks, which are built on internet protocol networks where voice operates as an application over the underlying data network.

It also warned that cheap, short-validity voice plans could lower the cost barrier for scammers and increase unsolicited commercial communications and fraud. Vodafone Idea warned that removing data from plans could expose users to unexpected charges. Background data consumption for activities such as software updates and OTP verification could trigger pay-as-you-go charges and result in bill shocks.

title: Trai Mandates Voice, SMS-only Affordable Plans
